title: MagoTech API
description: Hypermedia CRM API. Supports application/json (syntactic) and application/ld+json (JSON-LD/Hydra). All resource endpoints except GET /Api/ require a Bearer token (Authorization: Bearer {token}). Obtain one via POST https://mago.co/Api/Token with form-encoded grant_type=password&username=...&password=..., which answers 201 Created with the token in access_token (the legacy endpoint https://mago.co/Token answers 308 to the same place, preserving the POST body). An account whose subscription is not entitled is refused there with 402 Payment Required, exactly as the resources are.

supportedProperty.title: greeting

supportedProperty.title: exampleQuery

supportedClass.title: Access Token
supportedClass.description: A Personal Access Token grant at https://mago.co/Api/Token/Id/{id}. A token may READ its own grants - that is the only way a client can learn when its opaque credential expires - and may revoke one if it carries acl:Write. It can never MINT one, because minting requires the account password. Carries metadata only — name, scopes, expiry, last-used time, and owner. The secret NEVER appears here (enforced by https://mago.co/ns#AccessTokenResourceShape, which constrains https://mago.co/ns#secret to sh:maxCount 0), and the stored keyed hash has no representation at all. The identifier is a surrogate GUID, never anything derived from the secret. Grants are immutable: there is no PUT, because scope and expiry are fixed at creation.

supportedClass.title: Access Token Collection
supportedClass.description: The access-token grants visible to the caller at https://mago.co/Api/Token. Default-deny: a caller sees only their own grants. An administrator sees every grant across all users and may revoke any of them (this is scoped http://www.w3.org/ns/auth/acl#Control) — but no caller, administrator included, can read a secret, and no caller can mint a token for another user, because minting requires that user's own password.

supportedClass.title: Token Endpoint
supportedClass.description: Authentication for this API is a Personal Access Token presented as 'Authorization: Bearer {token}'. Mint one at https://mago.co/Api/Token (see https://mago.co/ns#AccessToken). The legacy endpoint https://mago.co/Token now answers 308 Permanent Redirect to https://mago.co/Api/Token, which preserves the POST method and body, so an existing form-encoded grant_type=password client keeps working. The token is an OPAQUE string prefixed 'mago_pat_' — it is not a JWT and must not be decoded; only a keyed hash of it is stored. Scope is expressed in W3C Web Access Control access modes (http://www.w3.org/ns/auth/acl#Read, .../acl#Write); a token lacking acl:Write is refused state-changing requests with 403. acl:Control is reserved for token administration and is never granted to a token. Minting answers 201 Created, with the secret in access_token and a Location header identifying the new grant. An account whose subscription is not entitled is refused here with 402 Payment Required rather than issued a token that no resource would honour. Tokens are revocable (DELETE the grant; effective on the next request), always expiring, and immutable — obtaining different scope means minting a new token. Legacy stateless JWTs issued before the cutover remain accepted until the announced acceptance cutoff and are then refused regardless of their own expiry.

supportedClass.title: Token Response
supportedClass.description: The response to POST https://mago.co/Api/Token — a strict superset of the OAuth 2.0 password-grant payload, so a client that only reads access_token is unaffected while an agent reads the same bytes as JSON-LD (the context aliases access_token to https://mago.co/ns#secret). This is the ONLY response that ever carries the plaintext secret; it is not stored and cannot be retrieved afterwards, so it must be captured here. Sent with Cache-Control: no-store.

supportedProperty.title: access_token
supportedProperty.description: The token string — include as 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}'. Opaque; do not decode. Shown exactly once.

supportedProperty.title: expires_in

supportedProperty.title: userName
supportedProperty.description: The account the token acts as. Retained because the v1 token endpoint returned it.

supportedProperty.title: tokenHint

supportedProperty.title: lastUsed

supportedProperty.title: acl:agent
